scene.note: Each test hands its answer to expect(), which throws a message that says what was wanted and what came.

steps.note: A test asks quote.js to price 250 cards in one colour.
expect() gets the quote, and toBe compares it with the price Sefton wrote down.
When they are not the same value, toBe throws, and the message names both prices.
The runner already turns that throw into a failed result, with the message kept.
A test asks for the printed quote of 100 invites: setup, printing and total.
The answer is a new object, so it can never be the very same object Sefton wrote.
toEqual compares what the two objects hold instead: the same keys, and equal values under each, all the way down.
Only a real difference throws, with both objects in the message.
A test wants a quote for a mug, which the press does not print, to be refused.
expect() gets a function that asks for the mug quote, and toThrow calls it.
quote.js throws, and its message says the item is unknown. That is the outcome the test wants.
Had the quote come back instead, toThrow would throw its own error, and the test would fail.
